_README: A single hand-kept Super Two cutoff for the season named below.
Before MLB Trade Rumors / the Associated Press publish the figure, this
is a guess and the site shows a range (computed low, this number high).
Once they publish it, set official to true: the site shows this number
and it decides who is Super Two. Past seasons live in
data/reference_super_two.json.
This project's own computed cutoff (scripts/super_two.py) has missed the
eventual published figure by a handful of days in every season checked
so far -- see scripts/validate_super_two.py. While official is false,
the site shows a RANGE rather than one number with false precision.
FIELDS
season   -- the season just played (NOT the offseason label), matching
reference_super_two.json's convention. If this does not
equal the season super_two.py's cutoff was measured from,
the site ignores this file and falls back to the single
computed cutoff -- so an entry only ever applies to the
offseason it was written for.
cutoff   -- years.days, e.g. "2.132". Parsed the same way every other
service-time figure on this site is (service_time.days_per_credited_year
from config/cba/, never a literal 172).
source   -- a short, honest note on where the number came from.
official -- true once MLB Trade Rumors / the Associated Press have
published the figure. An official figure is the line the
site shows and the line that decides Super Two eligibility.
Omit it, or leave it false, while the number is still a
guess: the site then keeps the computed-to-reported range
and does not move who qualifies.
entered  -- the date this row was added or last updated.
To update for a new offseason: replace season/cutoff/source/entered below.
To remove the high end entirely (show only the single computed cutoff),
delete this file or set season to a value that will not match -- either
way the site falls back gracefully, it does not error.
source: official: MLB Trade Rumors / Associated Press, November 2026
